summary: The note describes how residents of the Maplewood neighborhood are using technology to strengthen community life through a series of initiatives launched between September 2023 and April 2024. These cover community networking, safety, education, micro-business, health, digital inclusion, accessibility and sustainability, with municipal support from Councilmember Rajiv Singh. The central message is that people, not the technology itself, shape the community.
one_line: Maplewood residents launch apps and programs from 2023 to 2024 that use technology to build community, safety, inclusion, health and sustainability.
key_facts: Jenna Peterson launched the app "Maplewood Connect" on September 5, 2023, describing it as a "digital town square" for organizing events, community gardens and mutual support.

A neighborhood-wide surveillance system was initiated on October 15, 2023, with technical guidance from IT expert Arun Mehta, using affordable smart cameras that stream to a secure cloud database accessible only to authorized community members.
Arun Mehta says the camera network deters criminals and has helped create a digital neighborhood watch program.
Sarah Thomas, a librarian at the Maplewood Public Library, started a program on November 22, 2023 providing tablets and e-readers to children and adults, funded by grants and donations.
The library program offers learning workshops, coding classes for kids and digital literacy programs for seniors.
Veronica Chu began selling handcrafted jewelry on Instagram on December 3, 2023, giving rise to "Maplewood Creations," a collective of neighborhood creatives.
Mark Johnson introduced "FitMaplewood" on January 20, 2024, a virtual platform with live-streamed yoga, meditation classes and remote health consultations.
The "Maplewood Digital Inclusion Project," led by Brenda Lee, kicked off on February 25, 2024 and has supplied dozens of households with Wi-Fi access, computers and tablets.
The "Accessible Maplewood Initiative," led by Lucas Gomez, began on March 18, 2024 and worked with tech companies to install voice-activated systems and navigation aids.
Emily Song launched the "Green Tech Maplewood" campaign on April 21, 2024, promoting smart energy use, solar panels on communal buildings and an app to reduce the neighborhood carbon footprint.
Councilmember Rajiv Singh, an advocate for tech-based community development, is working with neighborhood leaders to align municipal resources with these projects.
The note concludes that it is "not the technology itself, but the people it empowers" that shapes the heartbeat of communities.
